name: Quarter-viewport list overscan

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
## Smaller list layer overscan

Mechanism: a list's layer holds 0.15 viewports of rows on each side of those shown (was 0.5), so fewer rows keep scenes, records and layout nodes. Rows still enter the layer as the scroll reveals them, so steady scrolling paints as many rows per frame as before. Allowed: the constant, its test-only override. Forbidden: div layers, tiles.
measurementPlanMarkdown: bm.sh over scroll-uniform-list, scroll-variable-list, scroll-data-table, 3 reps, against a fresh run of HEAD (also tried 0.25 and 0.1). Pass: heap peak down at least 5% on the three, CPU not worse, list-layer, memory and oracle tests green.

measurements.metric: scroll-data-table on heap peak / footprint MB
scroll-uniform-list on heap peak / footprint MB
scroll-variable-list on heap peak / footprint MB

measurements.delta: 0.25: heap -10% data-table; 0.1: -18% but variable-list draw p50 +12%

reportMarkdown:
## Smaller list layer overscan Finished

Passed: true at 0.15, a balance: 0.25 gains less memory, 0.1 slows `scroll-variable-list`. The overscan was a pure memory cost in steady scrolling, as rows come into the layer as they are revealed; it only pays a scroll that turns back. The scripted list-layer tests spell out a six-row viewport with three rows of overscan, so under `cfg(test)` they keep 0.5 through `list_overscan_viewports()`, and the memory tests (`fast::tests::layer_memory`) run at the shipped value. Tests: list_layers (64), layer_memory (4), oracle (17) pass; fmt and clippy clean.

Attempt Count: 1. Out-of-scope changes: none (a test-only override in paint.rs).
decisionMarkdown:
### Decision

Committed success. Remaining footprint above 1.3x is the tile textures (about 26 MB) and the third drawable (16 MB) at 120 fps.
